Home pitch for Panathinaikos, [ 51 ] AEK Athens [ 52 ] (football; Super League Greece, UEFA Champions League ), Greece national football team (some matches), International football competitions; [ 53 ] Track & Field events (e.g. IAAF Athens Grand Prix [ 54 ] ), Concerts [ 55 ] [ 56 ] [ 57 ]
Home court for Panathinaikos BC [ 58 ] and AEK BC [ 59 ] ( Greek basketball league ); Greece men's national basketball team, International basketball competitions, [ 60 ] Concerts [ 61 ] [ 62 ]
Swimming, Diving, Synchronized Swimming, Water Polo
Domestic and international swimming meets, [ 63 ] [ 64 ] [ 65 ] Public pool, [ 66 ] domestic league and European water-polo games.
Domestic and international tennis matches, training courts open to the public and home of the Athens Tennis Academy, currently the best-kept facility in the complex [ 67 ] [ 68 ]
Home court for Olympiacos BC (basketball), [ 70 ] Concerts, Conventions and trade shows [ 71 ]
Home court for Panionios BC (basketball), [ 72 ] Conventions and trade shows [ 66 ]
Turned over to a private consortium (J&P AVAX, GEP, Corfu Waterparks and BIOTER). Plans to convert it to a water park never materialised, [ 73 ] [ 74 ] and as of 2014 it sits abandoned. [ 75 ]

Originally planned to be part of new Hellinikon metropolitan park complex, but these plans never materialised. [ 76 ] As of 2017, abandoned, and with damaged turf. [ 77 ] [ circular reference ] [ 78 ]

Currently abandoned. Main ground (no. 1) initially converted to football pitch, home field of Ethnikos Piraeus F.C. (Football; Greek second division ), [ 79 ] auxiliary ground (no. 2) abandoned. In 2014, Ethnikos Piraeus F.C. moved grounds to the Peace And Friendship stadium, leaving the main ground abandoned.
Currently out of use, turned over to the private sector (Seirios AE), will become marina with 1,000+ yacht capacity [ 80 ] and will be part of Athens' revitalized waterfront [ 81 ]
TV filming facility, [ 66 ] Future home of the Hellenic Academy of Culture and Hellenic Digital Archive [ 82 ] [ 83 ]

Concert and theater venue, it hosted Helena Paparizou's concert on 13 August 2005 to celebrate the first anniversary of the Olympic Games. [ 84 ] Plans to turn it into an ultra-modern outdoor theatre never materialised, and as of 2024, the facility stands abandoned and vandalised. [ 66 ] [ 85 ]
Converted to the Athens International Convention Center, hosts concerts, conventions and trade shows [ 66 ] [ 83 ] [ 86 ] [ 87 ] [ 88 ]

After 2004, was the home court of AEK BC (basketball) before the team moved to the Athens Olympic Indoor Hall. Turned over to the private sector (Acropol Haragionis AE and Sonae Sierra SGPS S.A), being converted to a shopping mall and retail/entertainment complex. [ 89 ]
Now the site of the ultra-modern Badminton Theater, hosting major theatrical productions [ 90 ] [ 91 ]
Horse racing, [ 92 ] Domestic and International Equestrian meets, [ 93 ] [ 94 ] Auto racing (rallye) [ 95 ]
Converted to the official shooting range and training center of the Hellenic Police. [ 80 ] [ 96 ]

Has hosted fencing competitions in the years following the Olympics, [ 66 ] but has recently been turned over to the University of Piraeus for use as an academic lecture and conference center. [ 83 ] [ 97 ]
Part of the Parnitha National Park. In public use for biking and hiking. [ 98 ] [ 99 ]
Partially converted to a football pitch, also in use for gymnastics competitions. [ 66 ]
Schinias Olympic Rowing and Canoeing Centre

One of only three FISA -approved training centers in the world, the others being in Munich and Seville. [ 80 ] Hosts mainly domestic rowing and canoeing meetings. [ 100 ] [ 101 ] Part of the Schinias National Park, completely reconstructed by the German company Hochtief. [ 66 ]
Temporary facility, not in existence presently.

Home pitch for Iraklis (football; Super League Greece) [ 102 ] and temporary home pitch for Apollon Kalamarias FC (football; Greek second division). [ 103 ] Also in use for track and field meets. [ 104 ] Hosted the 2007 Greek football All-Star Game.
Home pitch for Olympiacos (football; Super League Greece) [ 105 ] and for the Greece National Football team. Also used as a concert venue.

Home pitch for Panahaiki (football; Greek third division ). [ 106 ] Also used for various track-and-field events, concerts, conventions, and friendly matches of the Greece National Football Team. [ 66 ]
Home pitch for OFI [ 107 ] [ 108 ] and Ergotelis (football; Greek Super League). [ 108 ] [ 109 ] Hosted the 2005 Greek football All-Star game. Also home to various track-and-field meets. [ 66 ]
Home pitch for Niki Volos (football; Greek third division). [ 66 ] Has also hosted concerts, conventions and track-and-field meets. [ 66 ]
Site of the first modern Olympic Games in 1896. One of Athens' major tourist attractions, also used for occasional sporting and concert events. [ 110 ] [ 111 ] [ 112 ] [ 113 ]
One of Greece's historic sites and largest tourist attractions, open to the public to this day. [ 114 ]

Half of it (the section fronting Kifissias Avenue ) has been turned over to the private company Lambda Development SA and has been converted to a luxury shopping, retail, office and entertainment complex known as the "Golden Hall". [ 115 ] The remaining section, facing the Olympic Stadium itself, will become home to the Hellenic Olympic Museum and the International Museum of Classical Athletics. [ 66 ] [ 83 ] [ 116 ]

2,292 apartments were sold to low-income individuals and today the village is home to over 8,000 residents. [ 66 ] Several communal installations however are abandoned and heavily vandalised. Only half of the apartments were ever sold, and significantly fewer schools ended up being built than initially promised, thereby resulting in residents facing significant journeys to take their children to schools. Most of the shops to serve the village's residents closed within months of the Olympics finishing, and concerns were raised over sewage, damp and building material quality. [ 117 ]
It has been turned over to the private sector and namely Lamda Developments S.A. (the same company which owns and runs the Mall of Athens and the Golden Hall), and has been converted to luxury flats.
